reason: Both responses gate high-stakes alerts and lean on reviewed templates. Response 1 better serves safe expansion because it names each harm with who is affected and the worst case, pairs each harm with a verification row (positive and negative controls, owner-set thresholds, stop conditions, publish blocking enforced in code), and routes the specific legal questions to counsel. Response 2 is more operationally practical, adding reader error reporting and a correction-and-resend process, but its evaluation plan lacks explicit controls or pass thresholds and it raises legal duties only as a question back to the team.
